wu: Warm-up: 'Work Values' word association. Students stand in a circle, say one job-related value (e.g., 'hard work'), and pass a ball to the next student who adds another (e.g., 'teamwork'). Continue for 2 minutes.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Job Charades'—students act out a profession (e.g., 'doctor') while others guess.
Alternative 2: 'My Dream Job'—quick share: 'I want to be a ___ because ___.'
pres: Presentation: Show 2 PET-style speaking task cards (e.g., 'Should unpaid internships be banned?'). Model a 1-minute opinion with reasons: 'I think yes because...'. Elicit feedback on structure (opinion + 2 reasons).
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'For/Against' T-chart on board—fill with student ideas.
Alternative 2: 'Internship Dilemma' short story—discuss the moral dilemma.
prac: Guided practice: 'Opinion Relay'—pairs take turns saying a sentence for/against unpaid internships using target phrases (e.g., 'On one hand... / On the other hand...'). Monitor and correct errors.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Builder'—use cut-up phrases to form full opinions.
Alternative 2: 'Thumbs Up/Down'—vote on statements, then justify.
ls: Listening slot: PET-style listening—short debate clip (2 mins) about internships. Students tick 'for' or 'against' reasons on a worksheet. Check answers in pairs.
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand for Values'—teacher reads statements (e.g., 'Unpaid internships exploit workers'). Students stand if they agree, sit if they disagree. Discuss briefly.
prod: Production task: Individual PET speaking assessment—students present a 2-minute opinion on 'Should unpaid internships be banned?' with 2 reasons. Teacher scores using a rubric.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Final PET reading (multiple-choice questions on a short text about Labour Day). Then write an 80-word email: 'Apply for an unpaid internship—include your opinion on it.'
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Play 'The Intern' short video clip (3 mins) showing a success story. Close with: 'Today we assessed your English skills and discussed work values. Thank you for your hard work this year!'
g: Teams guess jobs from clues (e.g., 'saves lives').
First to write 3 for/against reasons wins.
Call out job-related words—students mark them.
Students interview each other for a dream job.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 100-word paragraph on 'The best job for Morocco's future.'
Support: Use sentence starters (e.g., 'I believe... because...') for the speaking task.
hw: Option 1: Review your PET writing—highlight 3 improvements.
Option 2: Interview a family member about their first job.
Option 3: Write 5 sentences about Labour Day in Morocco.
tip: Use the assessment as a confidence booster—highlight progress made. In Morocco, connect Labour Day to local workers' contributions.
checklist: I can give my opinion with 2 reasons in a short talk.
I can understand a short debate about work.
I can write an 80-word email applying for a job.
I can read a short text and answer multiple-choice questions.
I can use phrases like 'On one hand...' to present arguments.
I can talk about my dream job using future tense.
I can identify key values in the workplace (e.g., respect, fairness).
